cards.alt: Sample multiple choice card: Glucose + Pi gives glucose 6-phosphate with delta G naught prime of +3.3 kcal/mol. ATP hydrolysis is -7.3 kcal

questions.stem: A reaction has a standard delta G of +4.2 kcal/mol. It is coupled to ATP hydrolysis (-7.3 kcal/mol). What is the delta G of the coupled reaction?
questions.explanation: Coupled reactions add: +4.2 + (-7.3) = -3.1 kcal/mol, so it is favorable. +11.5 and -11.5 result from adding magnitudes with the wrong signs, and +3.1 flips the sign of the sum.
questions.subtopic: Bioenergetics: free energy, coupling, ATP as energy currency

questions.stem: How many high-energy phosphate bonds are consumed to make one glucose from two pyruvate?
questions.explanation: Two pyruvate carboxylase steps use 2 ATP, two PEPCK steps use 2 GTP, and two phosphoglycerate kinase steps in reverse use 2 ATP, totaling 6 (4 ATP and 2 GTP).

questions.stem: A child has hepatomegaly and fasting hypoglycemia, and glycogen has a normal structure. Which enzyme is the most likely defect?
questions.explanation: G6Pase deficiency (von Gierke) causes hypoglycemia with massive hepatomegaly and normal glycogen structure. Branching enzyme gives abnormal structure, Pompe affects lysosomes and the heart, and muscle phosphorylase affects muscle only.

questions.stem: A patient on a statin has a markedly lower hepatic cholesterol synthesis rate. Which compensatory change is expected?
questions.explanation: Low sterol activates SREBP-2 processing, which raises LDL receptor expression and clears more LDL from plasma, lowering LDL. Reductase transcription rises, not falls, and SREBP-2 processing increases rather than decreases.

questions.stem: A person has fasted for 5 days. Compared with day 1, which change is expected?
options: Greater brain use of ketone bodies
questions.explanation: By day 5 ketones are the major brain fuel, and nitrogen loss is reduced. Liver glycogen is gone, ketones are high, and insulin is low.

demo_cards.front: What does the sign of delta G tell you about a reaction?
demo_cards.back: Negative delta G means exergonic and spontaneous as written. Positive means endergonic and needs energy input. Zero means equilibrium.

demo_cards.text: Actual free energy change: delta G = delta G naught prime + {{c1::RT ln Q}}. At equilibrium, delta G equals {{c2::zero}} and Q equals {{c2::Keq}}.
demo_cards.extra: Q is the reaction quotient, products over reactants at current concentrations.

demo_cards.stem: Which compound has a more negative hydrolysis delta G than ATP and rapidly regenerates ATP in resting muscle?
demo_cards.why: Phosphocreatine (about -10.3 kcal/mol) donates its phosphate to ADP via creatine kinase. Glucose 6-phosphate and glycerol 3-phosphate are low-energy phosphate esters.

demo_cards.statement: An enzyme makes a reaction more spontaneous by lowering its delta G.
demo_cards.why: Enzymes lower activation energy only. delta G and Keq are unchanged, so the enzyme speeds both directions equally.
